name: Interactive terminal/TUI
definition: Human-operated conversational terminal interface.
comparison_question: Can a human run and steer the harness interactively from a terminal?

name: IDE integration
definition: First-party or supported editor integration.
comparison_question: Is the harness available beside the code in an IDE?

name: Desktop or web surface
definition: First-party GUI or browser surface sharing the agent backend or sessions.
comparison_question: Can a human manage work through a GUI or browser?

name: Agent-native file editing
definition: The in-harness model can inspect and mutate files through governed tools.
comparison_question: Can the model directly edit repository files?

name: Agent-native shell execution
definition: The in-harness model can invoke shell commands or equivalent execution tools.
comparison_question: Can the model run commands?

name: Headless/non-interactive execution
definition: A supported one-shot or scripted interface without an interactive TUI.
comparison_question: Can an external agent or CI runner invoke the harness non-interactively?

name: Machine-readable output
definition: JSON, JSONL, event streams, or schema-constrained result output.
comparison_question: Can software reliably parse progress and final results?

name: Embeddable SDK
definition: Supported language SDK exposing the agent loop or harness runtime.
comparison_question: Can an application embed/control the harness through a supported SDK?

name: RPC/app-server protocol
definition: Versioned machine protocol for controlling sessions, turns, and events.
comparison_question: Can an orchestrator control the harness through RPC rather than terminal scraping?

name: MCP client
definition: Connects to Model Context Protocol servers for tools or context.
comparison_question: Can the harness discover and invoke MCP tools?

name: Agent Skills
definition: Reusable instruction/resource bundles discoverable or invokable by the model.
comparison_question: Can reusable skills be installed and used by the agent?

name: Plugins/extensions
definition: Installable packages that can add tools, skills, hooks, connectors, or UI.
comparison_question: Can functionality be packaged and distributed?

name: Lifecycle hooks
definition: User-defined code or policy at lifecycle events before/after tools, turns, or sessions.
comparison_question: Can deterministic automation intercept the agent lifecycle?

name: Hierarchical project instructions
definition: Repository- and directory-scoped instruction files loaded automatically.
comparison_question: Can projects carry durable, scoped instructions?

name: Dynamic context injection
definition: Context can be loaded at runtime by hooks, skills, tools, or routing logic.
comparison_question: Can context be selected dynamically rather than always preloaded?

name: Persistent memory
definition: Cross-session memory or learned knowledge managed by the harness.
comparison_question: Does the harness preserve and retrieve durable memory?

name: Resume, fork, and session lineage
definition: Sessions can be resumed, branched, named, or traced through lineage.
comparison_question: Can work continue without rebuilding context?

name: Subagents/delegation
definition: A primary agent can delegate bounded work to child agents.
comparison_question: Can the model create or direct subagents?

name: Parallel/background agents
definition: Multiple agent tasks can run concurrently or independently in the background.
comparison_question: Can long-running work continue without blocking the main session?

name: Cross-session agent messaging
definition: Running sessions can discover and send messages to one another.
comparison_question: Can separate sessions communicate natively?

name: First-class multi-agent coordination
definition: Coordination primitives beyond simple one-off delegation, such as teams, supervisors, or mixtures.
comparison_question: Does the harness provide explicit coordination semantics?

name: Remote/cloud execution
definition: Tasks or sessions can run remotely and be observed or resumed locally.
comparison_question: Can work execute away from the local terminal?

name: Self-hosted worker/runtime
definition: The user can supply machines or containers as governed execution workers.
comparison_question: Can remote execution run on user-owned infrastructure?

name: CI/GitHub automation
definition: Supported integration for CI jobs, pull requests, issues, or repository events.
comparison_question: Can the harness run safely in CI?

name: Scheduled tasks
definition: The platform can create or run recurring agent tasks.
comparison_question: Can agent work be scheduled without a human starting each run?

name: Execution sandbox
definition: OS/process/filesystem/network isolation for agent actions.
comparison_question: Are tool actions isolated from the host?

name: Granular permissions and approvals
definition: Fine-grained allow, deny, prompt, or policy controls for tools and commands.
comparison_question: Can operators define what actions require approval?

name: Enterprise managed policy
definition: Organization-admin controls, managed settings, identity, or policy enforcement.
comparison_question: Can administrators centrally govern the harness?

name: Usage and cost telemetry
definition: Tokens, cache, spend, quotas, or cost signals exposed to humans or software.
comparison_question: Can usage and spend be attributed?

name: Agent tracing/event telemetry
definition: Structured traces or events for turns, tools, agents, and outcomes.
comparison_question: Can executions be observed beyond terminal text?

name: Web search/research
definition: First-party or supported web search, fetch, grounded research, and citations.
comparison_question: Can the agent gather current web evidence?

name: Browser/computer use
definition: The agent can operate a browser or computer UI through supported tools.
comparison_question: Can the agent act through graphical applications?

name: Voice interaction
definition: Streaming speech input/output and conversational interruption support.
comparison_question: Can a human operate the agent by voice?

name: Artifacts, diffs, and rich result views
definition: Structured visual artifacts, diff inspection, or rich result viewers.
comparison_question: Can users inspect results beyond plain text?

name: Model/provider portability
definition: Multiple model providers can be selected without replacing the harness.
comparison_question: Can the same harness operate across providers?

name: Model and reasoning controls
definition: Model selection, effort, context-window, or routing controls exposed explicitly.
comparison_question: Can workflows pin and tune model behavior?

name: Output schema enforcement
definition: A JSON schema or equivalent can constrain the final output contract.
comparison_question: Can downstream automation rely on a validated result shape?

name: Programmatic human approval
definition: Approval decisions can be intercepted or supplied through a supported API/callback.
comparison_question: Can an application mediate risky actions rather than relying on terminal prompts?

name: Image generation
definition: The harness can produce a generated image file from a text prompt, natively or via a documented extension/tool it ships or supports — distinct from accepting an image as input.
comparison_question: Can the harness generate an image file from a text prompt, natively or via a documented extension/tool?
